findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping in getDocument query
findings.body: Any authenticated user can now retrieve another tenant's document simply by supplying its ID. The removed line `tenantId: ctx.user.tenantId,` was the only tenant isolation on this query; the surviving filter `where: { id }` (`src/documents.ts:33`, in `getDocument`) performs an ID-only lookup, so `db.documents.findFirst` will match and return documents belonging to other tenants. This is a cross-tenant authorization bypass / data-exposure regression that bites under realistic inputs (any enumerable or leaked document ID) and directly contradicts the PR's stated intent of preserving existing contracts. Restore the tenant filter, e.g. `where: { id, tenantId: ctx.user.tenantId }`.

markdown:
# PR Review

**Verdict:** request_changes

## Overview
This PR modifies `getDocument` in `src/documents.ts` by removing `tenantId: ctx.user.tenantId` from the `db.documents.findFirst` where clause, leaving the lookup filtered only by `id`. The authentication check (`if (!ctx.user) throw new UnauthorizedError()`) is retained.

Despite the PR description claiming to "preserve existing contracts," this change breaks the tenant-scoping contract of the document fetch: document access is no longer isolated per tenant. The single confirmed finding below is a blocking cross-tenant authorization regression.

## Verification
Verification was skipped: no user-level `verificationBaselines` are configured (`action: list` returned `enabled: false`), so there was no applicable trusted baseline to run. Note that baseline execution runs PR code unsandboxed (lifecycle supervision signals only the original POSIX process group; a deliberate `setsid`/session escape can survive it) — use an external sandbox or container wrapper when enabling verification for untrusted PRs.

## Findings

### [P1] Restore tenant scoping in getDocument query
**Severity:** P1
**Rationale:** Any authenticated user can now retrieve another tenant's document simply by supplying its ID. The removed line `tenantId: ctx.user.tenantId,` was the only tenant isolation on this query; the surviving filter `where: { id }` (`src/documents.ts:33`, in `getDocument`) performs an ID-only lookup, so `db.documents.findFirst` will match and return documents belonging to other tenants. This is a cross-tenant authorization bypass / data-exposure regression that bites under realistic inputs (any enumerable or leaked document ID) and directly contradicts the PR's stated intent of preserving existing contracts. Restore the tenant filter, e.g. `where: { id, tenantId: ctx.user.tenantId }`.
**Location:** `src/documents.ts:33 RIGHT`

## Lane completeness
The `conventions-maintainability`, `correctness`, and `performance-resources` lanes returned `partial` status (raw evidence: `NO FINDINGS`). Each was rerun with `review_subagent` under the same tool policy and returned identical raw evidence, and the orchestrator covered all three inline against the diff and surrounding file — no convention files exist, the one-line where-clause edit introduces no lifecycle/concurrency or resource concerns, and no additional findings were identified. `overview`, `correctness-contracts`, and `security-performance` completed fully.

## Strengths and notes
- The authentication guard (`if (!ctx.user) throw new UnauthorizedError()`) is preserved, and the change is minimal and easy to revert.
- Correctness: no state, ordering, async, or contract-compatibility issues beyond the tenant-scoping regression above.
- Security: the tenant-isolation removal is the sole security finding and is blocking.
- Performance: no regressions — the query remains a single indexed `findFirst`; removing a filter does not introduce leaks or unbounded work.
